Last night I watched the 2012 movie, Premium Rush, and I thought I'd give my impression for anyone who may be interested in seeing it.

The movie is based in the New York bicycle messenger culture. If you look up bike messengers on YouTube you'll find a lot of videos showing them tearing through traffic in New York, Chicago, LA, Rome, Paris and London, to name a few cities. In New York, they are a breed apart. They completely disregard the traffic laws. Astonishingly, they never seem to get hit by cars, or arrested.

The hero of the movie is a guy named Wilee (like in the Road Runner cartoons) who rides a "fixie" -- a fixed gear bicycle with no brakes. These bikes have taken off in popularity over the past five or six years. You can't coast on them, you have to keep pedalling all the time. The advantage of them is the unparalled control they give you. You can even ride backwards on them. The downside is (a) no gear changes, and (b) no brakes.

Riding a fixie is equated in the movie with bravery and with being a rebel. The main black character rides a regular road bike with three chain rings in front and dual brakes. He is presented as a prima donna and a bit of a wuss. The girlfriend of the hero rides a fixie, just like the hero, but she is not wholly dedicated to the fixie culture -- she put a front brake on her fixie, for security.

At one point the guy warns her that brakes are dangerous, and that her front brake is going to give her trouble. Sure enough, his words prove to be prophetic. She is riding along a street, sees some trash in front of her, and hits the front brake in a panic stop that sends her flying over the handle bars onto the asphalt. A little later she rips her front brake off her bike, calling it a "piece of crap," and throws it away. She is finally wholly committed to the fixie culture, and is now fit to ride with the hero.

I'm not going to bother getting into the plot of the movie. It's about a Chinese woman who needs to send a package to a certain woman in Chinatown in order to get her daughter into the United States. The drama comes as the hero tries to get the package across New York on his fixie, while being chased by a corrupt New York police detective who is on the take.

I'm not going to launch into a public safety tirade -- personally I don't give a fuck whether people ride with or without brakes, or helmets, or in the middle of sidewalks, or on the sides of buildings.

What I wanted to say is that the action sequences are amazing. The director was obviously taking notes from all the bike messenger documentaries on YouTube. The stuff in the movie is as good as the real thing, and it is almost impossible to tell that it was staged. The lead actor, Joseph Gorden-Levitt, actually seems to be able to ride a fixie. I mean, obviously he isn't performing the stunts, but he seems to be able to ride with skill.

Anyone fascinated by fixie culture, or impressed by the crazy daring of bike messengers in New York City, needs to watch this movie. It's a thrill ride from start to finish. The motivation is typical liberal horse shit ... get yet another immigrant into America, and win a gold star ... and of course the bad guy is a white male (who else?) but if you can keep your dinner down while being fed this liberal sewage, the action in the movie is first rate. I would recommend that any cyclist watch it. You'll enjoy it.
